items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I remember running into him at one of those jazz festivals in Colorado and I told him that story about Lester and he just fell out laughing and then he told me a beautiful story about Lester.

ctx.x: and I came to New York and that -- I got out of the war just about a month after it ended, August of 1945, and I ran into Lester again in '46 and of all places, would you believe it, 52nd Street. He's going the same way. He was going toward 6th Avenue, I was going towards 5th, and before he said, 'Hello, Bud, how are you,' he said, 'That Three Little Words was a bitch.' Now, you think of the memory of this, again not because it was about me, but the lovely thing to remember.
I told that to -- who is the bass player who has such a marvelous collection of Lester Young stories, is it Gene Ramey?
